mainTopic: The final משנה on women's mourning on festive days, followed by laments, comforting mourners, and who sits at the head.
overview: The amud opens with the last משנה of מועד קטן. On חול המועד women may wail but not clap (רבי ישמעאל lets those near the bier clap). On ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים they may wail and clap. A קינה is never allowed on any of these days, and after burial all of it stops. The משנה ends with ישעיהו's promise that death will be swallowed up forever. The גמרא asks what the wailing women said, and brings רב's lament and a list of sayings of the wise women of שכנציב quoted by רבא. רבי מאיר then teaches that whatever you do for the dead will be done for you. Next comes the story of the four elders who comforted רבי ישמעאל when his sons died. Each one makes a קל וחומר from a person with only one good deed who was still honored at death, and the גמרא clears up questions about צדקיהו, יאשיהו and the פסוק of הדדרימון along the way. The amud closes with laws of comforting: the mourner speaks first and sits at the head, a חתן and a כהן also sit at the head, and רבי חנינא begins a teaching on how hard death is that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Mourning on the intermediate days of the Festival
steps.stepSummary: On חול המועד women may wail but may not clap. רבי ישמעאל says those close to the bier may clap.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: On the Festival, women may wail but may not clap. רבי ישמעאל says: those who are close to the bier may clap.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the rule for חול המועד. Wailing is allowed, clapping is not, and רבי ישמעאל makes an exception for women standing near the bier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clapping is a stronger, more public sign of grief than wailing, so it clashes more with the joy of the מועד. The תנא קמא forbids clapping completely. רבי ישמעאל allows it for the women right next to the deceased, where the grief is most immediate.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the opening of the text)
Here, חול המועד: the intermediate days of פסח or סוכות
They clap their hands in mourning
The women close to the bier

phrases.english: MISHNA: On the Festival, women may wail,
phrases.notes: "The Festival" here means חול המועד, the in-between days.

phrases.english: but they may not clap.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
Those who are close to the bier may clap.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נָשִׁים בַּמּוֹעֵד מְעַנּוֹת, אֲבָל לֹא מְטַפְּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חול המועד: wailing is allowed and clapping is forbidden. רבי ישמעאל allows clapping for those near the bier.

steps.title: ראש חודש, חנוכה, פורים, and after burial
steps.stepSummary: On ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים women may wail and clap. On none of these days may they lament. After burial, no wailing or clapping is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ראשי חדשים, חנוכה and פורים they may wail and clap. On both kinds of days (מועד and these days) they may not lament. Once the deceased is buried, they neither wail nor clap.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to lighter days, where both wailing and clapping are allowed. It then gives two limits: a קינה is never allowed on any of these days, and all of it stops once the burial is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים carry less festive weight than חול המועד, so clapping is permitted on them too. A קינה, the strongest form of mourning, is still forbidden on every one of these days. After burial the mourning stops because these displays belong with the deceased, before he is buried.

keyTerms.meaning: On both this and that: חול המועד and the lighter days

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the three actions. Wailing (עינוי) and clapping (טפוח) are allowed on some of these days, but a קינה (lament) is not allowed on any of them.

phrases.english: On New Moons, on Chanukah and on Purim —
they may wail and clap;
on both this and that — they may not lament.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means both the Festival days from before and these lighter days.

phrases.english: Once the deceased has been buried —
they neither wail nor clap.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָאשֵׁי חֳדָשִׁים, בַּחֲנוּכָּה וּבְפוּרִים — מְעַנּוֹת וּמְטַפְּחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rules from חול המועד to lighter days and adds the limits of קינה and burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש חודש, חנוכה and פורים both wailing and clapping are allowed. A קינה is forbidden on all these days. After burial, no wailing or clapping is done.

steps.title: Defining wailing and lamenting
steps.stepSummary: עינוי means everyone wails together. קינה means one woman speaks and the rest answer after her, as the פסוק in ירמיהו shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is wailing? When they all respond together at once. What is a lament? When one speaks and they all answer after her, as it says: "Teach your daughters wailing, and each woman her neighbor lamentation."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines the two terms it has been using, so we know exactly what is allowed and what is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference lies in the form. In עינוי everyone wails at the same time. In קינה there is a leader and a group that answers her. The פסוק supports this: "each woman to her neighbor" pictures one woman passing the lament on to others.

keyTerms.meaning: Wailing: all the women wail together
Lament: one leads and the others answer

steps.whatToRemember: עינוי = everyone together (sometimes allowed). קינה = leader and response (never allowed on these days).

phrases.english: What is wailing?
When they all respond together at once.
A lament — when one speaks
and they all answer after her,
as it is stated:
"And teach your daughters wailing,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 9:19

phrases.english: and each woman her neighbor lamentation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the terms used in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עינוי is wailing all together. קינה is one woman leading and the others answering, based on ירמיהו 9:19.

steps.title: The future: death will be swallowed up forever
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends on a hopeful note: in the future, death will be destroyed and ה׳ will wipe away every tear.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about the future, the פסוק says: "He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord God will wipe away tears from every face," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: After all these laws of mourning, the משנה closes the מסכת with a comforting promise from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "but" (אבל) sets up the contrast. Today we need laws about how to wail and lament, but in the future there will be no death and no tears, so none of this will be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: In the time to come (the future redemption)

steps.whatToRemember: The מסכת ends with hope: mourning belongs to this world, and in the future ה׳ will end death and wipe away all tears.

phrases.english: But regarding the future, it says:
"He will swallow up death forever,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 25:8

phrases.english: and the Lord God will wipe away tears
from all faces," and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the mourning laws of this world with the future, when there will be no death.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Mourning belongs to this world. In the future, death will be destroyed and every tear wiped away.

steps.title: What do the mourning women say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what words the wailing women used.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What do they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking what the women actually said when they wailed. This line sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה told us when women may wail and lament, and how עינוי and קינה are done. It never said what words they used. The גמרא now fills in that missing detail.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה begins here

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What do they say?
phrases.notes: "They" means the women who wail and lament over the dead, from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's women's lament
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words spoken by the wailing women

steps.title: רב: Woe to the one who leaves and returns the pledge
steps.stepSummary: רב says the women cry, 'Woe to the one departing, woe to the one returning the pledge.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They say, 'Woe over the one who is going; woe over the one returning the pledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question with a short two-line lament the women would say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line mourns the person who is leaving this world. The second calls him one who returns a 'pledge': his soul was only lent to him for his life, and now he gives it back.

keyTerms.meaning: A pledge or deposit, here meaning the soul

phrases.english: Rav said:
Woe over him who is departing;
woe over him returning the pledge.
phrases.notes: The "pledge" is his soul, which was only on loan to him all his life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The women say: Woe to the one departing, woe to the one returning the pledge

steps.title: רבא: The women of שכנציב said the same lament
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that the women of שכנציב used the very same words as רב's lament.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say this: 'Woe over the one who is going; woe over the one returning the pledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up רב's version by reporting that the women of שכנציב said exactly the same thing. This also opens a list of their sayings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The women of שכנציב were known for their wisdom. Their use of the same words shows רב's lament was really used. From here רבא quotes more of their sayings.

keyTerms.meaning: The women of שכנציב, a town known for its wise women

phrases.english: Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say as follows:
Woe over him who is departing;
woe over him returning the pledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, נְשֵׁי דְּשַׁכְנְצִיב אֲמַרַן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches and supports רב's version of the lament
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The women of שכנציב used the same lament רב quoted

steps.title: The bone is taken from the jaw
steps.stepSummary: A saying about an old person who died: the bone is removed from the jaw and the water goes back to the kettle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say: 'The bone has been removed from the jaw, and the water returns to the kettle.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes another lament of the women of שכנציב, said over an elderly person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a picture, not a literal instruction. It was said over an elderly person who died. The גמרא does not explain the image further.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say:
The bone has been removed from the jaw
and the water returns to the kettle.
phrases.notes: This was said about an elderly person who died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another saying to רבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lament for an elderly person

steps.title: Cover the mountains for a noble person
steps.stepSummary: A lament calling on the mountains to wrap themselves in mourning, because the dead person came from great people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say: 'Wrap and cover yourselves, mountains, for he is the son of high and great people.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a lament for someone from an important family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the whole world, even the mountains, is told to dress in mourning. This shows how great the loss is.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrap yourself, as a mourner does

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say:
Wrap and cover the mountains in mourning,
as he is the son of the high and distinguished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another saying to רבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lament for someone from a distinguished family

steps.title: A fine cloak for a free man whose food ran out
steps.stepSummary: A lament about a once-wealthy man who lost everything: lend him a fine wool cloak as a burial shroud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say: 'Lend a cloak of fine wool to a free man whose provisions have run out.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a lament for a respected man who became poor and died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "cloak" is a shroud for burial. The point is that a proud, wealthy man who loses his fortune would rather die than live poor.

keyTerms.meaning: A free man, a person of standing
His provisions, his food for the road

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say:
Lend out a cloak of fine wool
phrases.notes: The cloak here is meant as his burial shroud.

phrases.english: for a free man whose provisions have run out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another saying to רבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lament for a respected man who lost his wealth

steps.title: Running, falling at the crossing, and borrowing
steps.stepSummary: A saying about a person who runs and falls at the river crossing and still has to borrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say: 'He runs and falls at the crossing, and borrows a loan.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes another short saying of the women of שכנציב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not explain this saying. It paints a picture of a person always rushing and stumbling, and still needing to borrow.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say:
He runs and tumbles at the ford
and still he borrows a loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another saying to רבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A saying about life's rushing and borrowing

steps.title: Our brothers the merchants will be examined
steps.stepSummary: A saying that the dead, like merchants, will have their dealings checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say: 'Our brothers, the merchants, will be examined at their stalls.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a saying comparing people to merchants whose business will be inspected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a merchant's stall is checked to see if he dealt honestly, every person's life will be examined. It reminds mourners that judgment comes after death.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say:
Our brothers, the merchants, will be examined at their places of business.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another saying to רבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every person's dealings will be examined

steps.title: Death is death, and sickness is like interest
steps.stepSummary: The last saying: everyone must die, and the suffering before death is like interest added to a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The women of שכנציב would say: 'Death is like death, and illnesses are like interest.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא ends the list with one more saying of the women of שכנציב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death itself is the same for everyone; no one escapes it. Illness and suffering are an extra payment on top, like interest added to a loan.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא answers 'what do the women say?' with רב's lament and a list of short sayings from the wise women of שכנציב, all quoted by רבא.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
The women of Shekhantziv would say:
Death is like death,
phrases.notes: Meaning everyone has to die; that part is the same for all.

phrases.english: and suffering is like interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final saying in רבא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Death comes to all; suffering is an extra payment like interest

steps.title: What you do for others will be done for you
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains the פסוק 'It is better to go to the house of mourning' as teaching that whatever a person does for the dead will later be done for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי מאיר used to say about the פסוק 'It is better to go to the house of mourning... and the living will take it to heart': what should he take to heart? Matters of death. Whoever eulogizes others will be eulogized. Whoever buries others will be buried. Whoever loads up praise in his eulogies will have praise loaded up for him. Whoever raises his voice in weeping for others will have voices raised for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר explains what 'the living will take to heart' means when visiting a house of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the living should 'take it to heart,' and רבי מאיר spells out what that is. You will get back exactly what you give the dead: הספד, burial, words of praise, and crying. Each pair is the same verb, first active and then passive, to show that it comes back measure for measure.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
One who eulogizes will be eulogized
One who 'loads' praise will have praise loaded for him
One who raises his voice will have voices raised for him

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a strong reason to take part in הספד and burial. One day others will do the same for you.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say:
"It is better to go to the house of mourning, etc."
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:2

phrases.english: until "and the living will take it to heart"
— matters of death:
one who eulogizes will be eulogized,
one who buries will be buried,
one who loads will be loaded for,
phrases.notes: Someone who 'loads' his eulogies with lots of praise will have others do the same for him.

phrases.english: one who raises his voice will have voices raised for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the laments in steps 6-13 to a new ברייתא about the lesson of a house of mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What a person does for the dead (הספד, burial, praise, weeping) will be done for him in return.

steps.title: Another version: one who does not raise himself will be raised
steps.stepSummary: Some read the last line differently: one who does not lift himself up in pride will be lifted up by others, as the פסוק in משלי teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: one who does not raise himself up will be raised up by others, as it is written: 'For it is better that they say to you, come up here...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רבי מאיר's last line. Instead of being about crying, it is about humility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ידל can mean 'raise.' In this version it means raising yourself in pride. If you hold back from pushing yourself up, others will lift you up. The פסוק in משלי backs this up: it is better to be invited higher than to grab a high seat and be sent down.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: an alternate version
One who does not raise himself up

phrases.english: And some say:
one who does not raise himself will be raised by others,
as it is written: "For it is better that it be said to you,
'Come up here,' etc."
phrases.notes: משלי 25:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the final line of רבי מאיר's teaching in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who stays humble and does not raise himself will be raised up by others.

steps.title: Four elders come to comfort רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that when רבי ישמעאל's sons died, four elders came to comfort him. רבי טרפון tells them not to interrupt each other, and רבי עקיבא says he will speak last.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When the sons of רבי ישמעאל died, four elders came to comfort him: רבי טרפון, רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and רבי עקיבא. רבי טרפון said to them: Know that he is a great sage and an expert in אגדות. None of you should cut into the words of his friend. רבי עקיבא said: And I will be last.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about comforting a mourner. This step sets the scene and the ground rules before the speeches that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל is a master of אגדה, so the comforters must speak carefully. Each one should finish his own words and not break into another's. רבי עקיבא chooses to speak last. That sets up the order of the comforting speeches.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
Into the words of his friend: interrupting

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁמֵּתוּ בָּנָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: When the sons of Rabbi Yishmael died,
four elders came in to comfort him,
Rabbi Tarfon, and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Tarfon said to them:
Know that he is a great sage
and an expert in aggadot,
let none of you enter
into the words of his friend.
Rabbi Akiva said: And I will be last.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֶׁמֵּתוּ בָּנָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about comforting mourners, separate from רבי מאיר's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting the scene: the comforters will each speak in turn without interrupting, and רבי עקיבא will speak last.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל blames his own sins
steps.stepSummary: The mourner, רבי ישמעאל, speaks first. He says his sins were many, so his losses came one after another, and he has troubled his teachers to comfort him twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל opened and said: His sins are many, his mournings came one right after another, and he troubled his teachers once and a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: Before the comforters speak, the mourner himself opens. He speaks about himself, as if about someone else, and takes the blame for his losses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads his repeated losses as a sign of his own sins. He also feels bad that his great teachers had to come comfort him a second time. This opening gives the comforters something to answer, and their speeches will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: His mournings came one right after another

steps.confusionAlert: 'His sins' and 'his teachers' are about רבי ישמעאל himself. He speaks about himself as 'he' out of humility.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael opened and said:
His sins are many, his mournings came one after another,
he troubled his teachers
a first time and a second.
phrases.notes: He means this is the second time his teachers have had to come comfort him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 16: the mourner speaks first, before the comforters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל blames his many sins for his repeated losses and for troubling his teachers twice.

steps.title: רבי טרפון comforts with the example of נדב ואביהוא
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says: if all of Israel cried over נדב ואביהוא, who did only one recorded מצוה, then all the more so should they cry over רבי ישמעאל's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון answered and said: The פסוק says, 'And your brothers, the whole house of Israel, shall weep over the burning.' Isn't this a קל וחומר? If נדב ואביהוא, who did only one מצוה, as it says, 'And the sons of אהרן brought the blood to him,' got this honor, then the sons of רבי ישמעאל deserve it all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: The first comforter, רבי טרפון, now speaks. He shows רבי ישמעאל that all of Israel should mourn his sons, using a קל וחומר from נדב ואביהוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says all of Israel cried for נדב ואביהוא. The Torah records only one מצוה they did: bringing the blood to אהרן. If one מצוה earned them a whole nation's tears, then רבי ישמעאל's sons, who did many מצוות, surely deserve the same.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a smaller case to a bigger one: if it is true here, it is surely true there
Burning; here, the fire that killed נדב ואביהוא
The two sons of אהרן who died by fire from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי טרפון is comparing רבי ישמעאל's sons to sinners. He is only saying: if even people with just one recorded מצוה got this honor, people with many מצוות surely deserve it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon answered and said:
"And your brothers, the whole house of Israel,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:6. This was said about the death of אהרן's sons.

phrases.english: shall weep over the burning."
Is this not a case of קל וחומר?
Now if Nadav and Avihu,
who did only one מצוה,
as it is written:
"And the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:9.

phrases.english: received this,
then the sons of Rabbi Yishmael
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי ישמעאל spoke first (Step 17), the first elder, רבי טרפון, begins the words of comfort.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of Israel should mourn רבי ישמעאל's sons, learned by קל וחומר from נדב ואביהוא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי comforts with the example of אביה בן ירבעם
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: if all of Israel mourned and buried אביה בן ירבעם, who did only one good thing, then all the more so should they mourn רבי ישמעאל's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי answered and said: The פסוק says, 'And all Israel shall mourn for him and bury him.' Isn't this a קל וחומר? If אביה בן ירבעם, who did only one good thing, as it says about him, 'because there was found in him a good thing,' got this honor, then the sons of רבי ישמעאל deserve it all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: The second comforter, רבי יוסי הגלילי, speaks. He uses the same kind of קל וחומר, this time from אביה, the son of the wicked king ירבעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביה came from a wicked family, yet the פסוק says all of Israel would mourn and bury him because of one good thing in him. If one good deed earned that honor, רבי ישמעאל's sons, full of good deeds, surely deserve it more. This speech sets up the גמרא's question in the next step about what that one good thing was.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will eulogize / mourn for him
אביה, son of King ירבעם, who died young

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili answered and said:
"And all Israel shall mourn for him and bury him,"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 14:13. This is said about אביה, son of ירבעם.

phrases.english: Is this not a case of קל וחומר?
Now if Aviyah son of Yeravam,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה אֶלָּא דָּבָר אֶחָד טוֹב,
phrases.english: who did only one good thing,
as it is written about him:
"Because there was found in him a good thing,"
received this,
then the sons of Rabbi Yishmael
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second elder gives a parallel קל וחומר, following the same pattern as רבי טרפון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of Israel should mourn and bury רבי ישמעאל's sons, learned by קל וחומר from אביה בן ירבעם.

steps.title: What was Aviyah's one good thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses the story to ask what the one good thing was that אביה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the good thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the ברייתא for a moment to ask a side question. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'a good thing was found in him' without saying what it was. The גמרא wants to know what deed earned אביה such honor.

keyTerms.meaning: A good thing / a good deed
The king who split from the kingdom of יהודה and stopped people from going to ירושלים

phrases.english: What was the good thing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in the פסוק that רבי יוסי הגלילי quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was the one good deed of אביה בן ירבעם?

steps.title: Two views: he left his guard post, or he removed the guards
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא and רבי חיננא בר פפא disagree. One says אביה left his own guard post and went up for the רגל. The other says he removed the guards his father had placed on the roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא and רבי חיננא בר פפא: One said, he left his guard post and went up for the רגל. The other said, he removed the guards that his father ירבעם had placed on the roads so that Israel would not go up for the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Both agree the good deed had to do with going up to ירושלים for the רגל, but they differ on what exactly he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view, אביה only helped himself: he left his post and went up. In the second view, he did something bigger: he took away the guards so that all of Israel could go up. Either way, he broke from his father's plan to block the pilgrimage.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up to ירושלים for the festival
Guards / guard posts placed along the roads

steps.whatToRemember: The one good deed of אביה was connected to letting people go up to ירושלים for the רגל: either he went himself, or he removed the guards for everyone.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Ḥinnana bar Pappa disagree:
One said: that he left his guard post
phrases.notes: His father had made him one of the guards stopping people from going to ירושלים.

phrases.english: and went up for the festival,
and one said: that he removed the guards
that Yeravam his father had placed on the roads
so that Israel would not go up for the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא וְרַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either אביה left his own guard post to go up for the רגל, or he removed all the guards his father placed on the roads.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה comforts with the example of King צדקיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: if צדקיהו was promised a peaceful death with royal honors for one מצוה, pulling ירמיה out of the mud, then all the more so do רבי ישמעאל's sons deserve honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answered and said: The פסוק says, 'You shall die in peace, and like the burnings for your fathers, the earlier kings who were before you, so shall they burn for you.' Isn't this a קל וחומר? If צדקיהו king of יהודה, who did only one מצוה, raising ירמיה out of the mud, got this, then the sons of רבי ישמעאל deserve it all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא returns to the comforters, and the third elder, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, speaks. He uses the same קל וחומר pattern with King צדקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צדקיהו was promised a peaceful death and honors like earlier kings. The one מצוה credited to him here is that he had ירמיה pulled out of the muddy pit. If one מצוה earned that, רבי ישמעאל's sons, with many מצוות, surely deserve honor and peace.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnings done in honor of a king at his death
The last king of יהודה before the destruction of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: Each elder used the same pattern: a person known for just one good deed still got honor at death, so רבי ישמעאל's sons, with many good deeds, deserve it all the more.

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah answered and said:
"You shall die in peace,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 34:5. This is said to King צדקיהו.

phrases.english: and like the burnings for your fathers,
the earlier kings
who were before you, so
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets finish the פסוק; some versions don't have them here.

phrases.english: shall they burn for you,"
Is this not a case of קל וחומר?
Now if Tzidkiyahu, king of Judah,
who did only one מצוה,
that he raised Jeremiah out of the mud,
received this,
then the sons of Rabbi Yishmael
all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about אביה, the ברייתא returns to the comforters with the third elder's speech.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל's sons deserve a peaceful death and honor, learned by קל וחומר from צדקיהו.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא quotes a verse about a great mourning
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא, the next speaker in the story, opens his words by quoting a פסוק from זכריה about a great mourning in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא answered and said: "On that day the mourning in ירושלים will be great, like the mourning of הדדרימון in the valley of מגידו."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא is the next רב to speak about the sons of רבי ישמעאל. He starts by quoting a פסוק, and this sets up his קל וחומר that comes a little later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the speakers before him, רבי עקיבא will compare the sons to someone the תורה says was mourned greatly. But the פסוק he quotes is unclear, because it is not obvious who הדדרימון is. So the גמרא first stops to explain the פסוק before finishing his argument.

keyTerms.meaning: a name in the פסוק; the Targum explains who he was

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva answered and said:
"On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great,
phrases.notes: זכריה 12:11

phrases.english: like the mourning of Hadadrimmon [in the valley of Megiddo]."
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets finish the פסוק. Some versions of the text add them here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth elder speaks in the same series of words of comfort to רבי ישמעאל, as he said he would (ואני אחרון).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא brings the פסוק of the great mourning 'like Hadadrimmon' as the base for his comparison.

steps.title: רב יוסף says the verse is only understood through its Aramaic translation
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף comments that without the תרגום of this פסוק, we would not know what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: Had it not been for the Aramaic translation of this verse, I would not have known what it is saying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story to add a comment from רב יוסף. He admits the פסוק is hard to understand without its תרגום, and this sets up the quote of the תרגום in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nowhere in תנ״ך do we read about a mourning for someone called הדדרימון. רב יוסף tells us the key to the פסוק is the תרגום, which fills in the missing story.

keyTerms.meaning: the Aramaic translation of the פסוק (here, תרגום יונתן)

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
Had it not been for the translation of this verse,
I would not have known what it is saying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment that explains the פסוק רבי עקיבא just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק of Hadadrimmon cannot be understood without its Aramaic translation.

steps.title: The תרגום explains the verse: אחאב and יאשיהו
steps.stepSummary: The תרגום says the פסוק refers to two great mournings. One was for אחאב, killed by הדדרימון. The other was for יאשיהו, killed by פרעה in the valley of מגידו.
steps.simpleTranslation: At that time the mourning in ירושלים will be as great as the mourning for אחאב בן עמרי, whom הדדרימון בן טברימון killed, and like the mourning for יאשיהו בן אמון, whom פרעה the lame killed in the valley of מגידו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the תרגום that רב יוסף mentioned. It shows the פסוק is really talking about two famous mournings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרגום splits the פסוק into two parts. הדדרימון is the man who killed אחאב, and the valley of מגידו is where יאשיהו was killed. This tells us that אחאב was mourned greatly, and that is the fact רבי עקיבא needs for his קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: אחאב son of עמרי, king of Israel
יאשיהו son of אמון, king of Judah

steps.whyThisMatters: Without this translation, רבי עקיבא's comparison would make no sense. The תרגום is what links the פסוק to אחאב.

phrases.english: At that time
the mourning in Jerusalem will be great
like the mourning for Ahab son of Omri,
whom Hadadrimmon son of Tabrimmon killed,
phrases.notes: So הדדרימון in the פסוק is the killer, not the person being mourned.

phrases.english: and like the mourning for Yoshiyahu son of Amon,
whom Pharaoh the lame killed
in the valley of Megiddo.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the תרגום that רב יוסף referred to, solving the puzzle of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes the mourning for אחאב (killed by Hadadrimmon) and for יאשיהו (killed at Megiddo).

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר from אחאב
steps.stepSummary: אחאב did only one good thing, keeping himself propped up in his chariot facing ארם, and he was still mourned greatly. So רבי ישמעאל's sons deserve great mourning all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this not a קל וחומר? If אחאב king of Israel, who did only one good thing, as it is written, "And the king was propped up in the chariot facing ארם," was mourned like this, then the sons of רבי ישמעאל all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי עקיבא finishes his argument. He uses the great mourning for אחאב to build a קל וחומר about רבי ישמעאל's sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as steps 18, 19 and 22: a person with only one recorded good deed got great honor, so righteous people surely deserve more. אחאב's good deed was staying upright in his chariot while wounded so the army would not see him fall and run away.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון, רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא all make the same kind of קל וחומר. Each one says that someone with only one good deed was honored, so רבי ישמעאל's righteous sons deserve even more.

phrases.english: Are these matters not a kal vachomer?
If Ahab, king of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא עָשָׂה אֶלָּא דָּבָר אֶחָד טוֹב,
phrases.english: who did only one good thing,
as it is written:
"And the king was propped up in the chariot facing Aram"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:35

phrases.english: was mourned like this,
phrases.notes: 'Like this' points back to the great mourning described in the פסוק from זכריה.

phrases.english: then the sons of Rabbi Yishmael,
all the more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side explanation of the פסוק, the גמרא returns to finish רבי עקיבא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since אחאב, with one good deed, was mourned greatly, רבי ישמעאל's sons deserve even greater mourning.

steps.title: How could צדקיהו die in peace if he was blinded?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out a contradiction. One פסוק promises צדקיהו 'you will die in peace', but another says his eyes were put out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רבה בר מרי: It is written about צדקיהו, "You will die in peace," and it is also written, "And he blinded צדקיהו's eyes"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק about צדקיהו from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's statement in step 22. רבא asks how a blinded captive can be called someone who 'died in peace'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 relied on the promise 'בשלום תמות' as a reward for צדקיהו. But נבוכדנצר blinded him and took him to Babylon, which hardly sounds peaceful. So the two פסוקים seem to clash.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:
It is written about Tzidkiyahu, "You will die in peace,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 34:5

phrases.english: and it is written, "And he blinded Tzidkiyahu's eyes"!
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 39:7

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ בְּצִדְקִיָּהוּ בְּשָׁלוֹם תָּמוּת וּכְתִיב וְאֶת עֵינֵי צִדְקִיָּהוּ עִוֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the צדקיהו פסוק used in step 22 and raises a contradiction between פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being blinded and exiled contradicts dying in peace.

steps.title: In peace means נבוכדנצר died first
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי יוחנן, רבה בר מרי answers that 'in peace' means צדקיהו lived to see נבוכדנצר die.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוחנן said this: it means that נבוכדנצר died in his lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי answers רבא's question using a teaching of רבי יוחנן. He explains what 'in peace' really means for צדקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that צדקיהו was blinded. Instead it redefines 'peace'. He had the comfort of seeing his enemy נבוכדנצר die before him, so he died with peace of mind.

keyTerms.meaning: the king of Babylon who blinded צדקיהו

steps.whatToRemember: The promise to צדקיהו holds true. Even though he was blinded, he died 'in peace' because he lived to see נבוכדנצר die.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yochanan said this:
that Nebuchadnezzar died in his lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word 'peace' in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In peace' means a calm death free of suffering, which clashes with his blinding.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In peace' means he outlived נבוכדנצר, so both פסוקים are true.

steps.title: How could יאשיהו die 'in peace' if he was shot full of arrows?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רבה בר מרי a second contradiction. One פסוק promises יאשיהו he will be buried 'in peace', but another פסוק says archers shot him, and רב says they made him like a sieve.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said to רבה בר מרי: It is written about יאשיהו: 'Therefore I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace.' But it is also written: 'And the archers shot at King יאשיהו,' and רב יהודה said in the name of רב that they made him like a sieve!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a second question of the same kind as the one about צדקיהו. A פסוק promised יאשיהו a peaceful death, but he was actually killed by many arrows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says יאשיהו will die 'בשלום'. The second פסוק, together with רב's explanation, shows a violent death with arrows everywhere in his body. The challenge is that these two facts seem to cancel each other out.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous king of יהודה, killed in battle by פרעה's army
You will be gathered to your grave, meaning you will die and be buried
Like a sieve, full of holes

phrases.english: And Rava said to Rabba bar Mari:
It is written about Yoshiyahu:
"Therefore, behold, I will gather you to your fathers,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 22:20

phrases.english: "and you will be gathered to your grave in peace,"
and it is written: "And the archers shot at King Yoshiyahu,"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 35:23

phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
that they made him like a sieve!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא לְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ בְּיֹאשִׁיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same type of contradiction as Step 27 about צדקיהו, now applied to יאשיהו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The promise to יאשיהו that he would die 'בשלום' (מלכים ב 22:20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A death by many arrows, described as being made 'like a sieve', cannot be called a death 'in peace'.

steps.title: 'In peace' means he did not see the בית המקדש destroyed
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר מרי answers in the name of רבי יוחנן. 'In peace' means the בית המקדש was not destroyed during יאשיהו's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: 'In peace' means that the בית המקדש was not destroyed in his days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר מרי resolves the contradiction by explaining what 'in peace' really means for יאשיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שלום' is not about how יאשיהו's body died. It means he was spared from living through the destruction of the בית המקדש. This is the same kind of answer as Step 28: 'peace' refers to what the king did or did not live to see, not to a gentle death.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what רבי יוחנן said
In his days, during his lifetime

steps.whatToRemember: In both kings' cases, 'dying in peace' is explained by what they lived or did not live to see. צדקיהו saw נבוכדנצר die, and יאשיהו did not see the בית המקדש destroyed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
that the Beis HaMikdash was not destroyed in his days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק: 'שלום' refers to national events in his lifetime, not to the way he died.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In peace' would mean a calm, non-violent death.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In peace' means the בית המקדש stood for his whole life, so there is no contradiction with his violent death.

steps.title: Comforters must wait for the mourner to speak first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the laws of comforting mourners. רבי יוחנן teaches that comforters may not speak until the אבל speaks first, and he proves it from איוב and his friends.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Comforters are not allowed to say anything until the mourner speaks first. As it says: 'After this, איוב opened his mouth,' and only afterward: 'And אליפז the Temanite answered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of the kings and goes back to the laws of ניחום אבלים. רבי יוחנן gives a rule about who speaks first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב's friends sat with him silently. Only after איוב himself spoke did אליפז begin to answer. From this order of events, רבי יוחנן learns that the comforters must wait for the mourner to open the conversation.

keyTerms.meaning: Comforters, the people who come to console a mourner

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה followed at every שבעה visit: visitors wait for the אבל to speak first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Comforters are not permitted to say anything
until the mourner opens (speaks first),

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַחֲרֵי כֵן פָּתַח אִיּוֹב אֶת פִּיהוּ״,
phrases.english: as it is said: "After this, Iyov opened his mouth,"
phrases.notes: איוב 3:1

phrases.english: and only afterward: "And Eliphaz the Temanite answered."
phrases.notes: איוב 4:1

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין מְנַחֲמִין רַשָּׁאִין לוֹמַר דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the kings and returns to the laws of comforting mourners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comforters may not speak until the mourner speaks first, learned from the order of speaking in ספר איוב.

steps.title: The mourner sits at the head
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that the אבל sits at the head, and he learns it from a פסוק in איוב that connects sitting 'at the head' with mourners being comforted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: From where do we know that the mourner reclines at the head? As it says: 'I chose their way and sat as head, and dwelt like a king among the troops, as one who comforts mourners.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds another rule about mourners: the אבל takes the seat at the head. He backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions sitting as 'ראש' (head) in the same breath as comforting mourners. רבי אבהו reads this as a source that the mourner is the one placed at the head of the gathering.

keyTerms.meaning: Reclines, sits at a meal or gathering
At the head, in the place of honor

steps.whatToRemember: Two rules for a שבעה visit: the אבל speaks first (רבי יוחנן), and the אבל sits at the head (רבי אבהו).

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
From where do we know that the mourner reclines at the head?
As it is said: "I chose their way and sat as head,"
phrases.notes: איוב 29:25

phrases.english: "and dwelt like a king among the troops,"
"as one who comforts mourners."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מִנַּיִן לָאָבֵל שֶׁמֵּיסֵב בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another law of comforting mourners, again learned from ספר איוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourner sits at the head, learned from איוב 29:25.

steps.title: The word in the פסוק seems to describe the comforter, not the mourner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's proof. The word ינחם in the פסוק from איוב sounds like 'he comforts others,' which would mean the comforter sits at the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'יְנַחֵם' means he comforts others!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof רבי אבהו just brought. It says the word in his פסוק points the wrong way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו learned from the פסוק that the person sitting 'at the head' is the אבל. But if you read ינחם as 'he will comfort,' the person at the head is the one doing the comforting. That would mean the comforter sits at the head, which is the opposite of רבי אבהו's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He will comfort (others): the active reading of the word

phrases.english: 'Yenachem' means that he comforts others!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of רבי אבהו in step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's proof from the פסוק in איוב that the אבל sits at the head
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verb ינחם reads as active, 'he comforts,' so the one at the head would be the comforter and not the mourner.

steps.title: The word is written so it can be read as 'is comforted'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is written in a way that can be read יִנָּחֵם, 'he is comforted.' So the person at the head is the mourner after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is written 'יִנָּחֵם' (he is comforted).
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק saves רבי אבהו's proof by pointing to how the word is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of the word can also be read as יִנָּחֵם, which means 'he is comforted.' On that reading, the one sitting at the head is the one being comforted, which is the אבל. So the פסוק does support רבי אבהו.

keyTerms.meaning: He is comforted: the passive reading of the word

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the same letters. The difference is only in the vowels, and the written letters allow the passive reading 'is comforted.'

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
'Yinachem' is written.
phrases.notes: He means the word can be read as 'he is comforted,' so it describes the mourner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: ״יִנָּחֵם״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ינחם is active, so the one at the head is the comforter
steps.terutzMaskana: The word is written so it can be read as passive, 'is comforted,' so the one at the head is the אבל

steps.title: A second source: the mourner becomes a prince over those reclining
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא brings a different פסוק from עמוס to prove that the אבל sits at the head. He reads מרזח as the grieving mourner and סר as שר, a prince over those reclining around him.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: It comes from here: 'And the revelry of those who stretched out shall pass away.' The מרזח (the grieving one) becomes a prince over those who recline.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers another פסוק to prove the same rule that the אבל sits at the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the words in a new way. מרזח becomes מר, 'bitter,' plus זח, 'troubled,' which describes the grieving mourner. סר becomes שר, a prince, so the mourner is a prince over the comforters reclining around him.

keyTerms.meaning: From here: introduces a different source
Revelry. Here it is read as the bitter, troubled mourner
Those who stretch out, or recline

steps.whatToRemember: The אבל sits at the head. It is learned either from איוב (רבי אבהו, defended by רב נחמן בר יצחק) or from עמוס (מר זוטרא).

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: It is learned from here:
'And the revelry of those who stretched themselves out shall pass away.'
phrases.notes: עמוס 6:7

phrases.english: 'Mirzach,' the mourner, is made a prince over those who recline.
phrases.notes: He reads מרזח as מר (bitter) plus זח (troubled), and reads סר as שר, a prince.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the rule of step 32
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the אבל sits at the head
steps.raayaSupportSource: עמוס 6:7, read so that the mourner becomes a prince over those reclining

steps.title: A groom sits at the head, like a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא teaches that a חתן reclines at the head. He learns it from the פסוק 'כחתן יכהן פאר,' which links the חתן to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: How do we know that a groom reclines at the head? Because it says, 'Like a groom who decks himself (יכהן) with a garland.' Just as a כהן is at the head, so too a groom is at the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related seating rule: a חתן sits at the head of the table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יכהן sounds like כהן. So the פסוק compares the groom to a כהן. Since a כהן sits at the head, the groom does too.

keyTerms.meaning: Decks himself with a garland. יכהן is related to the word כהן
So too: introduces the second half of a comparison

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
From where do we know that a groom reclines at the head?
As it says: 'Like a groom who decks himself with a garland.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 61:10. The key word is יכהן, which sounds like כהן.

phrases.english: Just as a priest is at the head,
so too a groom is at the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: מִנַּיִן לְחָתָן שֶׁמֵּיסֵב בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new seating rule, connected to the theme of who sits at the head
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חתן reclines at the head, learned from the comparison to a כהן

steps.title: How do we know a כהן sits at the head?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that a כהן himself sits at the head, since the groom's rule depends on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the כהן himself, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step. It asks for the source of the basic rule about the כהן, which the groom's rule was built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חמא בר חנינא assumed a כהן sits at the head without giving a source. Before the comparison can work, the גמרא wants to know where that rule comes from.

phrases.english: And from where do we know this about the priest himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the assumption in step 36
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a כהן is placed first, at the head

steps.title: A כהן goes first in every matter of holiness
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from 'וקדשתו' that a כהן is honored first in every holy matter. He opens first, leads the blessing first, and takes the good portion first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And you shall make him holy.' This applies to every holy matter: to open first, to bless first, and to take a nice portion first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא that gives a כהן priority in all holy matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells us to treat the כהן as holy. The ברייתא explains that this means giving him first place in holy matters: reading the תורה first, leading ברכת המזון first, and taking the best portion first. This priority is why a כהן sits at the head, and so the groom does too.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
And you shall make him holy
To open first, meaning to read the תורה first
To bless first, meaning to lead ברכת המזון

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן gets first place in holy matters (וקדשתו). A חתן is compared to a כהן, so he sits at the head too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basic source for giving a כהן the first עליה and the honor of leading ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'And you shall sanctify him':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:8, talking about the כהן.

phrases.english: for every matter of holiness:
to open first,
phrases.notes: He means being the first to read from the תורה.

phrases.english: and to bless first,
and to take a nice portion first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'וקדשתו': a כהן gets priority in every holy matter, so he sits at the head

steps.title: The soul's leaving the body is hard
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא opens a teaching that the departure of the נשמה from the body is difficult. The comparison that finishes his sentence comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: The leaving of the soul from the body is as hard as...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes רבי חנינא, who says that dying, the soul leaving the body, is hard. This line sets up a comparison that comes next, telling us just how hard it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was talking about the honor of the mourner, the חתן and the כהן at a meal. Here it changes direction and goes back to death itself. רבי חנינא's sentence is not finished yet: the word קָשָׁה, 'hard,' is waiting for a comparison to show how hard.

keyTerms.meaning: The going out of the soul, meaning the moment of death

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at 'the soul's leaving is hard' as if that is the whole teaching. The sentence keeps going, and the next words give the comparison that is the real point.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The soul's departure from the body is as difficult

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: קָשָׁה יְצִיאַת נְשָׁמָה מִן הַגּוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of who reclines at the head (steps 32 to 38) and returns to the general subject of death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The departure of the soul from the body is difficult. The exact comparison follows in the continuation of the statement.
